failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_1 states 'To fully verify this claim, retrieval is needed for: 1. The complete identity of the author of the work "Love and Mr Lewisham" 2. The nationality of the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham"'. Summary_2 then states 'H. G. Wells is the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham"' and lists 'H. G. Wells' nationality (is he English or not?)' as missing. The hop 2 query targets this: 'Who is the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham"? What is the nationality of the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham"?' and hop 3 query includes 'H. G. Wells author Love and Mr Lewisham nationality English'. Despite these well-formed queries across multiple hops, no passage about H. G. Wells' nationality or biographical details was ever retrieved—only passages about other award-winning authors and unrelated topics.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_2 devotes significant analysis to passages about Lewisham borough, stating 'The passages do NOT contain: - H. G. Wells' nationality (is he English or not?)' after listing passages about 'Lewisham London Borough Council' [2], 'London Borough of Lewisham' [4], and 'Catford' [7] which are clearly about London geography and local government, not the author H. G. Wells. Time was spent documenting these irrelevant passages rather than focusing on the core missing evidence gap.

failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Who is the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham"? What is the nationality of the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham"? Was the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham" award-winning?' This is formulated as three natural-language yes/no and interrogative questions, bundling multiple targets together rather than as targeted entity-based search terms.
